TARGET 1.1: By 2030, eradicate extreme poverty for all people everywhere, currently measured as people living on less than $1.25 a day

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The heavy dependence on imported equipment, technology, and expertise for green hydrogen production and end-use poses a risk of limiting the economic benefits and job opportunities that could have been generated domestically. Additionally, if investments and policies related to green hydrogen prioritize foreign entities or neglect the inclusion of local communities, it has the potential to worsen existing disparities and hinder poverty reduction efforts. In the case of Africa, green hydrogen production can pose the highest risk (red flag) to the progress towards the target due to poor working conditions and lower gross domestic product/purchasing power parity per capita compared to those of other countries. In general, the ability to manufacture key equipment within the country reduces the risk of various social indicators closely related to this target, such as fair salaries and social security expenditures.

VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:

Additionally, if investments and policies related to green hydrogen prioritize foreign entities or neglect the inclusion of local communities, it has the potential to worsen existing disparities and hinder poverty reduction efforts. In the case of Africa, green hydrogen production can pose the highest risk (red flag) to the progress towards the target due to poor working conditions and lower gross domestic product/purchasing power parity per capita compared to those of other countries. In general, the ability to manufacture key equipment within the country reduces the risk of various social indicators closely related to this target, such as fair salaries and social security expenditures.

TARGET 1.5: By 2030, build the resilience of the poor and those in vulnerable situations and reduce their exposure and vulnerability to climate-related extreme events and other economic, social and environmental shocks and disasters

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain has positively potential to influence the adoption of various mitigation measures, drive the deployment of renewable energy technologies, facilitate the implementation of sustainable agriculture methods, enhance water management systems, seasonal storage, and establish governance frameworks that promote climate resilience. Green hydrogen production can increase renewable energy production capacity by replacing fossil fuels and decreasing greenhouse gas emissions. The transportation can provide system integration (e.g. seasonal storage) and avoid using fossil fuels, as seen in India. In the end-use, green hydrogen can decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors (e.g. steel, cement, chemical industry, refineries, and aluminum). All these actions can mitigate the potentially catastrophic impacts of climate change. Most countries have already worked on mitigation actions to 2030, using green hydrogen. To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain at the local level can provide clean energy solutions that mitigate climate-related risks and create local economic stability.

TARGET 10.2: By 2030, empower and promote the social, economic and political inclusion of all, irrespective of age, sex, disability, race, ethnicity, origin, religion or economic or other status

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Despite the increasing number of work opportunities for women in the green hydrogen value chain, the production of green hydrogen in low-income countries, such as Africa, poses a significant risk of widening the gender wage gap. This means that other possible actions to inclusion can also be affected considering age, sex.

TARGET 10.6: Ensure enhanced representation and voice for developing countries in decision-making in global international economic and financial institutions in order to deliver more effective, credible, accountable and legitimate institutions

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen represents a global value chain that has the potential to integrate the Global North and Global South, offering shared decision-making power (green flag).

TARGET 11.2: By 2030, provide access to safe, affordable, accessible and sustainable transport systems for all, improving road safety, notably by expanding public transport, with special attention to the needs of those in vulnerable situations, women, children, persons with disabilities and older persons

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "", "transportation": "", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen end-use can positively and indirectly contribute to the sustainable transport system by decreasing dependency on carbon-based fuels being used as a sustainable fuel, reducing pollution and preventing deaths and mitigating respiratory illnesses, particularly in the transport sector. There already are initiatives in public transportation which use green hydrogen as a fuel, such as in trains (Germany).

TARGET 11.6: By 2030, reduce the adverse per capita environmental impact of cities, including by paying special attention to air quality and municipal and other waste management

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can positively and indirectly contribute to reducing the adverse environmental impact of cities by decreasing dependency on carbon-based fuels, improving air quality in urban areas, facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources into urban infrastructure, and reducing emissions from transportation. Several initial hydrogen city projects have been developed, with more envisioned for the coming years, such as (South Korea 2022; Ornkey Island, Scotland (2023), Harumi Flag, Japan (2024); Noem, Saudi Arabia (2025), Wuhan, China (2030). To meet this target, transportation and end-use segments of the green hydrogen value chain can improve air quality and implement effective local and waste management practices.

TARGET 12.1: Implement the 10-year framework of programmes on sustainable consumption and production, all countries taking action, with developed countries taking the lead, taking into account the development and capabilities of developing countries

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen production can positively contribute to investments in renewables, aiding in reducing fossil fuel consumption, such as firewood and coal, particularly in developing countries. The end-use of green hydrogen, whether as green ammonia or fuel, can positively and indirectly influence and benefit other sectors such as agriculture and transportation. To meet this target, production and end-use segments of the green hydrogen value chain can reduce the environmental footprint and promote sustainability.

TARGET 12.2: By 2030, achieve the sustainable management and efficient use of natural resources

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The electrolyzer technology for producing green hydrogen requires scarce and expensive materials, such as platinum and iridium, in addition, to raw materials needed for constructing renewable sources (red flag). The end use of green hydrogen can indirectly influence large-scale industrial processes as an essential raw material (red flag). To meet this target, production and end-use segments of the green hydrogen value chain can promote the sustainable management and efficient utilisation of natural resources through renewable energy sourcing, resource efficiency, decarbonization, circular economy at the local level.

TARGET 12.6: Encourage companies, especially large and transnational companies, to adopt sustainable practices and to integrate sustainability information into their reporting cycle

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "", "transportation": "", "end_use": "direct_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can promote directly the development of sustainable business models and incentivize companies to invest in sustainable technologies and practices.

TARGET 12.7: Promote public procurement practices that are sustainable, in accordance with national policies and priorities

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen production and end-use applications can have positive and indirect influences on countries that adopt sustainable practices and technologies to tackle environmental concerns, fostering a more sustainable energy future.

TARGET 12.a: Support developing countries to strengthen their scientific and technological capacity to move towards more sustainable patterns of consumption and production

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": "direct_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen production in developing countries is increasingly seen for import rather than final use. The reliance on technology from other countries for hydrogen production. The cost of green hydrogen still prohibits developing countries from investing in this technology for their own end-use (red flag). To meet this target, the production and end-use segments of the green hydrogen value chain can support developing countries in developing their own technology at the local level.

TARGET 13.1: Strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards and natural disasters in all countries

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can promote the development and deployment of green hydrogen, which can contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions (e.g. decarbonization of these hard-to-abate sectors) and building resilience to climate-related hazards and natural disasters, mainly replacing fossil fuels (green flag). To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain can enhance adaptive capacity to climate change, provide sustainable energy solutions, and foster global collaboration in addressing climate-related challenges from the local level.

TARGET 13.2: Integrate climate change measures into national policies, strategies and planning

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The development and deployment of a green hydrogen value chain can indirectly promote fostering the integration of climate change measures into national policies and planning (green flag).

TARGET 14.1: By 2025, prevent and significantly reduce marine pollution of all kinds, in particular from land-based activities, including marine debris and nutrient pollution

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen end-use, as a fuel, can be an option for decarbonizing the maritime sector. However, the importation of green hydrogen may further increase the establishment of new trade routes and links in the coming years. Additionally, the costs associated with using green hydrogen as a fuel are expected to decrease, making it more competitive with other fuel options. The maritime sector can still be affected by port operations, offshore green hydrogen production, and the infrastructure required for green hydrogen transportation (red flag). To meet this target, the entire green hydrogen value chain can play a vital role in preventing and significantly reducing marine pollution, from production to end-use. Green ammonia stands as an exemplary fuel option for the maritime sector. In this case, the reciprocal interdependence approach is at a global level (e.g. the infrastructure and use of ports).

TARGET 14.2: By 2020, sustainably manage and protect marine and coastal ecosystems to avoid significant adverse impacts, including by strengthening their resilience, and take action for their restoration in order to achieve healthy and productive oceans

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen end-use, as a fuel, can be an option for decarbonizing the maritime sector. However, the importation of green hydrogen may further increase the establishment of new trade routes and links in the coming years. Additionally, the costs associated with using green hydrogen as a fuel are expected to decrease, making it more competitive with other fuel options. The maritime sector can still be affected by port operations, offshore green hydrogen production, and the infrastructure required for green hydrogen transportation (red flag). To meet this target, the presence of the entire green hydrogen value chain can contribute to strengthening resilience to avoid significant adverse impacts and taking action for their restoration to achieve healthy and productive oceans. In this case, the reciprocal interdependence approach is at a global level (e.g. the infrastructure and use of ports).

TARGET 15.5: Take urgent and significant action to reduce the degradation of natural habitats, halt the loss of biodiversity and, by 2020, protect and prevent the extinction of threatened species

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The new structure of the green hydrogen value chain can have initial negatively influences on natural habitats, including the deployment of renewable sources, construction of new pipelines, and raw mineral for batteries. While being regarded as having the least environmental impact, the implementation of a new supply chain still carries potential risks to the natural habitat.

TARGET 15.9: By 2020, integrate ecosystem and biodiversity values into national and local planning, development processes, poverty reduction strategies and accounts

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen end-use can promote sustainable land use practices, such as agriculture, through the use of green ammonia (green flag). To meet this target, the presence of the entire green hydrogen value chain can integrate ecosystem and biodiversity values into planning and development processes. Prioritizing sustainability ensures maximum benefits with a minimal ecological footprint at the local level.

TARGET 16.1: Significantly reduce all forms of violence and related death rates everywhere

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The production of green hydrogen through the utilization of renewable energy has the potential to indirectly trigger conflicts and tensions, notably regarding issues such as land acquisition, employment opportunities, and the absence of mechanisms for reinvesting project revenues within the local community (for instance, in Africa) – a situation warranting careful attention (red flag). In the same way, it can affect the transportation and end-use with the construction of new infrastructure urban, for example)

TARGET 17.1: Finance: Strengthen domestic resource mobilization, including through international support to developing countries, to improve domestic capacity for tax and other revenue collection

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can be harnessed to attract investments, generate tax revenue, and bolster domestic capacity in developing countries. However, it is crucial to amplify international support through technology transfer, partnerships, and knowledge sharing. Without such support, there is a risk that these countries might merely transform into exporters of green hydrogen, rather than fostering development through domestic resource mobilization and revenue collection (red flag).

TARGET 17.11: Trade: Significantly increase the exports of developing countries, in particular with a view to doubling the least developed countries’ share of global exports by 2020

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Large-scale green hydrogen production has the potential to be developed primarily in developing countries with the aim of exporting it. However, careful analysis is required for both the local market and the investments associated with this exportation. Additionally, the responsibility for transportation costs must be determined between the importer and exporter countries (red flag).

TARGET 17.12: Trade: Realize timely implementation of duty-free and quota-free market access on a lasting basis for all least developed countries, consistent with World Trade Organization decisions, including by ensuring that preferential rules of origin applicable to imports from least developed countries are transparent and simple, and contribute to facilitating market access

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen transportation is still in need of trade agreements, especially for large-scale transport of liquid hydrogen or the establishment of an international hydrogen pipeline grid, for example (red flag). This alignment and cooperation can facilitate market access for LDCs and foster equitable trade practices.

TARGET 17.14: Systemic issues - Policy and Institutional coherence: Enhance policy coherence for sustainable development

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can contribute to creating a clear and supportive policy environment for the development and deployment of green hydrogen technologies. This includes the establishment of supportive regulatory frameworks, incentives, and standards (green flag).

TARGET 17.16: Systemic issues - Multi-stakeholder partnerships: Enhance the global partnership for sustainable development, complemented by multi-stakeholder partnerships that mobilize and share knowledge, expertise, technology and financial resources, to support the achievement of the sustainable development goals in all countries, in particular developing countries

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can positively influence the multi-stakeholders parnterships since these partnerships facilitate the mobilization of financial resources, sharing of knowledge and expertise, and promotion of green hydrogen technologies adoption in all countries, especially in developing nations.

TARGET 17.19: Systemic issues - Data, monitoring and accountability: By 2030, build on existing initiatives to develop measurements of progress on sustainable development that complement gross domestic product, and support statistical capacity-building in developing countries

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can have a significant influence on ensuring that developing countries have access to the necessary data and tools for measuring progress on sustainable development (e.g. green certifications). It also plays a crucial role in developing effective policies and strategies (green flag).

TARGET 17.3: Finance: Mobilize additional financial resources for developing countries from multiple sources

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can mobilize additional financial resources for developing countries through a combination of investments, international funding, public-private partnerships, carbon market revenue, domestic revenue generation, technology transfer, and diplomatic agreements (green flags).

TARGET 17.4: Finance: Assist developing countries in attaining long-term debt sustainability through coordinated policies aimed at fostering debt financing, debt relief and debt restructuring, as appropriate, and address the external debt of highly indebted poor countries to reduce debt distress

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can attract international cooperation and support, and by reducing reliance on fossil fuel imports and promoting clean energy solutions, green hydrogen can contribute to reducing debt distress and fostering long-term sustainability in developing countries

TARGET 17.5: Finance: Adopt and implement investment promotion regimes for least developed countries

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain, least developed countries can strategically position themselves as appealing investment hubs. These strategies not only foster the expansion of the green hydrogen industry but also provide avenues for fostering sustainable economic progress and facilitating the transfer of advanced technologies (green flag).

TARGET 17.6: Technology: Enhance North-South, South-South and triangular regional and international cooperation on and access to science, technology and innovation and enhance knowledge sharing on mutually agreed terms, including through improved coordination among existing mechanisms, in particular at the United Nations level, and through a global technology facilitation mechanism

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can have a negative influence if the adoption and deployment of green hydrogen technologies are not connected with the sustainable development priorities mainly by exporting countries.

TARGET 17.7: Technology: Promote the development, transfer, dissemination and diffusion of environmentally sound technologies to developing countries on favourable terms, including on concessional and preferential terms, as mutually agreed

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can facilitate the local development and transfer of green hydrogen technologies to developing countries, such as renewables and electrolyzers. However, since this process involves international cooperation, particular attention must be given to this objective, as it raises a potential concern (red flag).

TARGET 17.9: Capacity-Building: Enhance international support for implementing effective and targeted capacity-building in developing countries to support national plans to implement all the sustainable development goals, including through North-South, South-South and triangular cooperation

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can offer opportunities for North-South, South-South, and triangular cooperation to enhance the capacity-building efforts of developing countries. However, these actions through technology transfer, educational programs, policy support, infrastructure development, and investment partnership must benefit both sides (green flags).
